item.title: Gears of War: E-Day uses SSD storage tech to cut RAM usage
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: We tested the RAM-saving storage tech in Gears of War: E-Day
Gears of War: E-Day uses storage technology to reduce RAM usage, leveraging NVMe SSDs as an extension of system memory. The Coalition dynamically loads complex city data in real time, balancing performance with smart data management. Testing showed that SATA SSDs caused visual degradation, while NVMe SSDs improved smoothness on lower-end systems with 16GB RAM. The game’s average read bandwidth exceeded SATA limits, leading to immersion issues. On high-end systems, NVMe SSDs saved about 2GB of RAM. The technology, similar to Windows’ virtual memory, allows developers to create dense worlds on limited hardware. Results suggest other developers may adopt similar methods for visually rich games on lower-end systems.

item.title: TV soundbar audio delay causes and fixes
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The reasons why your TV soundbar has an audio delay
Audio delay between TVs and soundbars occurs when video and audio signals aren't synchronized. Common causes include loose HDMI or optical cables, audio processing delays from TV and soundbar decoding, and HDMI ARC limitations. Solutions include tightening connections, disabling TV features like dynamic contrast or virtual surround sound, and adjusting audio sync settings. Samsung soundbars use the Sound Control remote with Audio Sync buttons, LG offers AV Sync, and Sonos users adjust settings in the app. Direct routing bypasses the TV by connecting devices directly to the soundbar. HDMI eARC upgrades resolve bandwidth issues for high-quality audio. Alternatively, switching to PCM or stereo audio reduces processing lag. Resetting devices or updating firmware may also resolve persistent delays.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: SD card limits file size to 4GB due to FAT32, fix explained
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why your SD card won't let you transfer files bigger than 4GB, and how to fix it
SD cards using FAT32 cannot transfer files larger than 4GB. This limitation stems from FAT32's 32-bit file size recording, which caps individual files at nearly 4GB. While the card's physical capacity may support larger files, the file system blocks them. To enable transfers of files over 4GB, users must reformat the card to exFAT, which supports larger files. Formatting steps vary by operating system: on Windows, open File Explorer, right-click the SD card, and select exFAT under File System. On macOS, use Disk Utility to erase the card with exFAT. Older devices may not support exFAT, requiring FAT32 instead. Windows restricts FAT32 formatting for cards larger than 32GB, necessitating third-party tools for such cases. Backing up data before formatting is recommended.

item.title: Original Xbox Celebrates 25th Anniversary with Promotions and Retro Hardware Details
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: The original Xbox was released 25 years ago today
Microsoft's original Xbox launched on November 15, 2001, during the sixth generation of consoles. It featured an Intel Pentium III 733 MHz CPU, Nvidia NV2A 233 MHz GPU, 64MB DDR SDRAM, and a built-in 8GB HDD. The console sold 24 million units, outperforming competitors like the PlayStation 2, Nintendo GameCube, and Sega Dreamcast. Halo: Combat Evolved was a key title that contributed to its success. Xbox Live online gaming launched in 2002, aided by an Ethernet port for broadband connectivity. The system ran a modified Windows 2000 OS. For its 25th anniversary, Microsoft offers free games, wallpapers, and in-game items. A limited-edition Xbox Series X25 in OG Green with 1TB SSD is available. Pre-built PCs with the 25th-anniversary bundle include 25 fan-favorite Xbox games. Anniversary promotions also include an Xbox account badge and exclusive content updates.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Samsung TV cache clearing fixes app crashes and lag
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to clear the cache on your Samsung TV
Clearing the cache on a Samsung TV can resolve performance issues like app crashes, lag, or buffering. Temporary cache files accumulate over time, affecting streaming apps like Netflix, Hulu, and YouTube. The process varies by TV model: newer models (2020+) use Settings > Support > Device Care > Start Device Care for full cache clearing, while older models (2016-2018) require alternative methods like deleting browser data. Clearing cache frees up storage space, though it may temporarily slow app launches and delay image loading. Users may also lose saved app preferences if they clear data instead of cache. A cold boot, achieved by holding the power button or unplugging the TV, can also reset the system. Regular cache clearing is recommended to maintain smooth operation.

item.title: Google Integrates Gemini with Wallet for Spending Tracking
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Gemini can now help you fix your bad spending habits if you use Google Wallet
Google announced on November 13 that Gemini can now analyze users' spending habits by integrating with Google Wallet and linked bank accounts. The feature, part of Personal Intelligence, allows users to review past expenses, create spending charts, and identify forgotten subscriptions or price increases. Users can access the tool on Android, iOS, and the web by connecting Wallet via Personal Intelligence and mentioning @Google Wallet in conversations. Gemini provides read-only access to financial data, cannot transfer funds or manage accounts, and does not directly use transaction data to train its AI models. However, summaries and inferences from transactions may be used for training when Keep Activity is enabled, and some interactions could involve human review. The integration is optional, and users can disconnect Wallet at any time.

item.title: This built-in Windows tool can diagnose your PC's battery health
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Powercfg is a built-in Windows tool that helps diagnose laptop battery health. It allows users to monitor battery performance and identify issues through command-line commands. To access Powercfg, open an administrator terminal and run commands like 'powercfg /batteryreport' to generate an HTML file detailing battery capacity and health. A full charge capacity below 40% indicates the need for replacement, according to Dell. Another command, 'powercfg /energy,' runs a 60-second efficiency check, producing a report highlighting power-draining apps or devices. The tool is particularly useful for laptops, where battery issues can affect performance and longevity. Users can locate the generated reports in specified file locations. Powercfg simplifies self-diagnosis of battery problems, helping determine when a replacement is necessary.

item.title: FAA Ground Stop Caused by Fiber Upgrade and Router Failure
item.description:
Source: The Verge, TechCrunch, Gizmodo Original headline: FAA Ground Stop Linked to Fiber Optic Upgrade and Router Failure
A nationwide ground stop halted thousands of U.S. flights on Friday after a routine FAA fiber optic upgrade triggered a router overload. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed the disruption to the switch from copper wiring to fiber at a remote FAA facility managed by L3Harris. The upgrade, described as 'routine maintenance,' caused the Air Traffic Control system to fail, leading to over 8,200 flight cancellations and an additional 3,000 affected on Saturday. FAA acting CTO Rebecca Guy noted the system experienced 'over 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds,' overwhelming communication channels. Officials confirmed the issue was an equipment malfunction, not a cyberattack, with no evidence of foreign interference. Duffy called for increased congressional funding to modernize aging infrastructure, noting the upgrade occurred during the day rather than overnight. L3Harris, which has completed 70% of the fiber conversion, is cooperating with the investigation. FAA administrator Bryan Bedford stated the outage was unrelated to an AI tool recently rolled out, which was not consulted with controllers' unions. The FAA is reviewing upgrade scheduling to prevent future disruptions.

item.title: Slack's Stewart Butterfield: Selling Organizational Transformation
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Quote of the day by Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield: 'What we are selling is not the software product… it's organizational transformation"
Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield described the service as selling 'organizational transformation' rather than just software. Founded as a video games company called Tiny Speck, the team developed an internal communication tool that became Slack. Butterfield's internal memo, later shared publicly, framed the product as a shift in how teams work, with benefits like reduced information overload, stress relief, and easier archive searches. Slack has maintained its identity after its $28 billion acquisition by Salesforce, adding features like MCP integration, 'big mode' for complex projects, and AI bots in channels. The company continues innovating with custom AI instructions and deeper research tools, positioning itself as an essential but flexible platform in the business software landscape.

item.title: Painting Wind Turbine Blades Black Reduces Bird Deaths by 70%
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Today I learned why wind farms paint one turbine blade black
Painting a single wind turbine blade black reduced bird deaths by 70% at Norway's Smøla wind farm. Researchers from the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research compared four turbines with one black blade to four standard ones over 10 years, publishing results in Ecology and Evolution. The change disrupted motion smearing, a phenomenon where birds perceive fast-moving blades as a single rotating circle. The intervention proved effective for white-tailed sea eagles but may not work for all species due to varying visual acuity. A Dutch trial tested red blades on offshore turbines, while a study at Aberdeen offshore wind farm found no bird collisions. The technique requires specialized crews and lifts, with costs and practicality considerations. Local bird populations and species-specific behaviors influence the effectiveness of such measures.

item.title: Doom Slayer Joins Rainbow Six Siege as Season 4 Skin
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'You can't just take any IP character and throw them in because it just doesn't work. That's where skin collaborations work' — The Doom Slayer is the latest gaming icon to join Rainbow Six Siege and will be fragging his way onto Season 4
Doom’s anti-hero, the Doom Slayer, will join Rainbow Six Siege as a skin for the Tachanka operator in Season 4, set to release December 22, 2026. The collaboration was revealed at the 2026 Majors tournament in Osaka by Creative Director Joshua Mills, with a teaser video showing the Slayer battling a Rainbow Six drone. The skin follows recent collaborations with Halo, Resident Evil, and Tomb Raider. Game Director Chris Budgens emphasized skins as a flexible way to integrate characters, noting Rainbow Six Siege has only one permanent operator from another universe—Solid Snake from Metal Gear Solid. Budgens explained that while Snake’s inclusion was a long-term goal, reimagining him as a Tom Clancy agent made him fit the game’s grounded universe. Mills highlighted the need for careful IP integration, stating, 'You can't just take any IP character and throw them in because it just doesn't work.' The Slayer’s skin marks a continuation of skin-based collaborations, though Mills hinted at future fully integrated third-party operators if properly rationalized.

item.title: Study links irregular sleep schedules to depression, anxiety; wearables may help track and improve patterns
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Research links poor sleep schedules with depression and anxiety. Your wearable could help fix it.
A study by researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, and the University of California, San Diego links irregular sleep-wake schedules to increased depression, anxiety, and loneliness. Analyzing data from 23,000 participants, the team found that lower Sleep Regularity Index (SRI) scores—ranging from 0 to 100—correlated with more severe symptoms. Participants with severe depressive symptoms averaged an SRI of 75, compared to 84 for those with few symptoms. Similar patterns were observed for anxiety and loneliness. The study highlights that wearables like smart rings can track sleep patterns and provide data-driven recommendations for improving sleep regularity. Researchers note the bidirectional relationship between sleep schedules and mental health, suggesting future work should test if correcting irregular sleep reduces symptoms. Wearables can also flag sleep disorders like apnea and offer tools to monitor and adjust sleep habits. The findings emphasize the potential of widely available technology to support mental health through sleep regulation.

item.title: BrickLink Restored After Data Breach Disruption
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Lego Marketplace BrickLink Back in Action After Data Breach
BrickLink, the world's largest Lego marketplace, was offline for nearly a week due to a data breach. Service resumed on November 12 after being taken down on November 5 to secure the platform. The company confirmed some usernames, IP addresses, and a small number of email addresses were accessed during the breach, but no passwords or payment information was compromised. Affected members will receive direct contact from BrickLink. The marketplace will waive seller fees for November and December as a result of the incident. The Studio Forum, its message board, remains offline. BrickLink, founded by Dan Jezek in 2000 and acquired by Lego Group in 2019, has 1.3 million registered users across 199 countries.

item.title: China Develops Drone to Administer Painkillers to Wounded Soldiers
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: China’s Air Force builds drone that shoots painkiller darts at wounded soldiers
China's Air Force Medical University developed a UAV capable of administering painkillers to wounded soldiers via darts, according to the Global Times. The drone, designed for battlefield use, can inject medication into injured personnel from a distance, buying time for treatment. Wang Jianqi, a university representative, stated the system allows remote delivery of life-saving drugs to soldiers' muscles. While the drone remains experimental due to challenges in assessing injuries and loading incapacitated patients, it aligns with modern battlefield medicine's 'golden hour' principle. The project reflects broader trends in drone use for military and civilian applications, including Ukraine's frontline operations. Historical context includes helicopter medevacs during World War II and MASH units in the Korean War, which improved survival rates. China's drone initiative aims to advance battlefield medical response, though practical deployment hurdles persist.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to Clear Xbox Series X Cache for Better Performance
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to clear the cache on your Xbox Series X
Clearing the cache on an Xbox Series X can improve performance by removing corrupted temporary files. The process involves unplugging the console for two minutes, then power-cycling it by pressing the power button multiple times before reconnecting. This resolves loading errors or connectivity issues, as noted by Epic Games in its support documentation. While clearing the cache doesn't affect games or save data, some users report temporary increases in loading times for titles like Microsoft Flight Simulator, though others note faster boot times. If issues persist, a console reset is recommended, with options to sync save data to the Xbox network or perform a factory reset. A factory reset wipes all unsynced data and requires re-downloading content, but may restore optimal performance for games. Routine cache clearing is advised when the console feels sluggish, though no fixed schedule is necessary.

item.title: Roku TV users report random power-ons linked to OS update
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Common reasons your Roku TV can turn on by itself and how to fix it
Roku TV users report random power-ons after August 2026 OS update 15.3. The update, which didn't involve autoplay or power management, may have introduced a bug causing TVs to turn on without input. HDMI-CEC, a feature linking A/V devices via HDMI, could trigger glitches if signals miscommunicate. Fast TV Start, a power-management setting, might also contribute by keeping the TV's OS active. Solutions include updating to OS 16, disabling HDMI-CEC and Fast TV Start, unplugging the TV, or using a smart plug. Roku hasn't officially identified the root cause.

item.title: Why some USB ports are yellow (and less common than others)
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Yellow USB-A ports typically indicate Always On charging, allowing devices to charge when a computer is off. However, this color is not an industry standard, as the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF) recommends blue for distinguishing USB versions, though manufacturers may use other colors. Lenovo used yellow for Always On ports on older models but later replaced them with battery icons. Yellow ports may not be the fastest option, with red generally offering higher speeds. Color coding for data transfer rates is inconsistent, and manufacturers vary in their implementation. Users should check labels, icons, or manuals to confirm a port's capabilities, as yellow ports may range from USB 2.0 to USB 3.0. USB-C ports increasingly omit color coding due to their single connector design. Always On functionality may require BIOS settings or AC power for activation.

item.title: Marvel Comics Launches Angela's First Solo Book in Over a Decade
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Marvel Comics Is Letting Angela Fly Once Again
Marvel Comics is launching Angela's first solo book in over a decade. Written by Wes Craig and drawn by Pere Pérez, the series follows Angela being sent to Earth to combat a demon outbreak in New York. The story explores her relationship with Heven and the demon lord Abraxas. Created in 1993 by Neil Gaiman and Todd McFarlane, Angela's rights were awarded to Gaiman after a legal dispute. She has appeared in various Marvel titles, including as a guest star and in team books. Craig describes Angela as a stoic, no-nonsense warrior and notes the challenge of revealing her vulnerabilities. The book will debut in February 2027 on shelves and digitally. Angela also joined the Marvel Rivals roster last year. Craig states the series will explore what would make Angela show her heart and break.

item.title: Mass Effect Composer Credits Collaboration for RPG Success
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'You can suddenly float to the 30,000-foot level and understand how it’s all supposed to work together' — Original Mass Effect composer looks back on the 'rewarding' collaborative experience while working on the RPG
Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall described the collaborative process for the RPG as 'rewarding,' emphasizing the value of working with other composers like Sam Hulick, Richard Jacques, and David Kates. Wall noted that teamwork helped fulfill the role of music as an 'unseen character' in the game, enhancing storytelling and player immersion. He explained that collaborating allowed for a more fluid creative process, enabling the team to 'float to the 30,000-foot level' and understand how elements align to serve the game's narrative. Wall, who also discussed the influence of orchestral and synth music on the series, highlighted that working with others made the project more efficient, offering 'instant gratification' by finishing music faster for refinement. He acknowledged his own strengths in storytelling but stressed that collaboration amplified the project's success, allowing for a '1 + 1 = 3' outcome. The composer also reflected on BioWare's closure, though the focus remained on the collaborative experience's impact on the game's musical identity.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: INSTRUCTION: iPhone Duo Tips: 9 Settings to Improve Usability
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Got an iPhone Duo? These 9 settings make it easier to use
Apple’s iPhone Duo lacks Face ID, requiring users to adapt to Touch ID for unlocking and authentication. To improve usability, users should register multiple fingerprints for Touch ID, enable Apple Watch unlock, and adjust volume controls to reorient with device rotation. A back-tap shortcut for screenshots and the Reachability feature can simplify one-handed use. A custom shortcut locks the screen when the device is folded. Camera controls can be personalized via the Camera app’s settings. These adjustments address challenges like limited screen reach and the absence of Face ID, making the Duo more user-friendly despite its unique form factor. Settings are accessible through the Settings app under Touch ID & Passcode, Sounds & Haptics, and Accessibility menus.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Fitbit Edge settings improve user experience and battery life
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Change these Fitbit Edge settings for a better experience
Google's Fitbit Edge offers customizable settings to enhance user experience. Key adjustments include changing the watch face for additional widgets, adjusting tracker orientation to prevent accidental button presses, and disabling Coach Insights to reduce distractions. Battery life can be extended by using phone GPS instead of the Edge's built-in GPS and turning off Always-On Display, which cuts battery life from seven days to around two. Daily charging with a 30W adapter can also help. The Edge is positioned as a budget-friendly alternative to smartwatches like the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Garmin Forerunner 570, focusing on fitness tracking without full smartwatch features.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 5 Affordable PCIe Cards Transform Old PCs into Premium NAS Systems
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 cheap PCIe cards that turn any old PC into a premium NAS
Five affordable PCIe cards can transform an old PC into a high-performance NAS. The 10Gtek 6-Port SATA 3.0 card expands storage with six SATA ports using ASMedia's ASM1166 chip, requiring an x4 PCIe slot. For more than six drives, SAS3008-based HBA cards like the 9300-8i offer server-grade performance, though they generate heat and require verification to avoid counterfeit parts. A 2.5GbE card, such as Intel's I226-V, upgrades Ethernet speed to 280MB/s, but network infrastructure must support the bandwidth. For faster data transfer, a 10GbE card like the Intel X520-DA2 provides 1,100MB/s throughput, ideal for large file transfers. A dual NVMe adapter like the GLOTRENDS PA20 adds NVMe storage with a built-in switch, bypassing PCIe bifurcation limitations. Users should prioritize SATA and 2.5GbE cards for a minimal setup, then add others as needed. Used PCs remain a cost-effective option for NAS builds.

item.title: Google Health Premium's Nutrition Tracking Simplifies Food Logging
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: This underrated Google Health app feature can make food tracking less annoying
Google Health Premium's Nutrition section simplifies food tracking by integrating with Fitbit and Pixel devices. Users can log meals via photo, barcode, or voice commands, with the app analyzing ingredients and calculating macros. The feature provides real-time calorie targets, burn rates, and progress toward dietary goals. Subscription costs $9.99 monthly or is included with Google One. It identifies eating patterns, like caffeine affecting sleep or meal timing impacting energy levels, and offers tailored recommendations. Users can review daily summaries showing remaining calorie allowances and macro percentages. Logging is streamlined through voice dictation or photo uploads, making it easier to track snacks and meals throughout the day.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Gets Animated Series 'Planeswalker'
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: The ‘Magic: The Gathering’ Show Is Real, and It’s Called ‘Planeswalker’
Magic: The Gathering is launching its first animated series, Planeswalker, at MagicCon: Atlanta. The show centers on Chandra, a fire-wielding Planeswalker hunted for her powers and haunted by her past. The synopsis describes a conflict between Planeswalkers against an insidious force, with stakes involving a cataclysmic war across multiple worlds. The series draws visual inspiration from Netflix's Arcane and Riot Games' League of Legends, featuring dynamic action sequences and art styles. Animation studio Digic Pictures, known for League of Legends cinematics and Blood of Dawnwalker, is involved. Planeswalker is set for a 2027 Netflix release. The reveal video included concept art and action scene renders, highlighting the show's cinematic approach.

item.title: NVIDIA GPU Comparison to PS5 Highlights Performance Gaps and Costs
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Which NVIDIA GPU is closest to the PS5? The answer isn't so simple
NVIDIA's RTX 2070 Super matches the base PS5's APU performance but is outdated, costing $280. The PS5 Pro, priced at $1,250, uses a custom AMD APU with improved GPU power. Newer GPUs like the RTX 5060 and RX 9060 XT outperform the PS5 Pro but require compatible CPUs and RAM. Comparisons are complex due to differences in architecture and system components. Digital Foundry notes the RTX 2070 Super can achieve PS5-level performance under optimal conditions, but PC builds demand more than just a GPU. The PS5 remains cost-effective for 4K gaming, while high-end PC setups offer cutting-edge features like 120 FPS path tracing. Both consoles deliver smooth 4K results, making them preferable for most users despite the PS5 Pro's higher price and limited availability.

item.title: Nvidia’s security team questioned over Megaspeed and CEO affairs
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Where was Nvidia’s security team?
Nvidia’s chief security officer, David Reber, stepped down in August citing health reasons, followed by CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation over allegations of extramarital relationships. Reber’s replacement, Saša Zdjelar, did not comment on the transition. The Megaspeed data center company, under U.S. investigation for allegedly shipping Nvidia chips to China, is linked to Huang’s relationships with employees. While no public connection exists between security team actions and the Megaspeed matter, experts question whether Nvidia’s security team was aware of government scrutiny or Huang’s affairs. Retired intelligence officer Nicholas Eftimiades noted security teams often lack resources and face challenges identifying risks from foreign intelligence exploitation. Nvidia’s top lawyer engaged with the Megaspeed inquiry over a year ago, and multiple employees reported knowledge of Huang’s relationships. However, it remains unclear if security teams acted on this information. Eftimiades emphasized that intelligence services prioritize policy insights over technology, with tactics like IMSI catchers used in past espionage cases. The board’s investigation and federal probes will clarify what Nvidia’s security team knew and whether it could have intervened.

item.title: Lawyer upgrades AI server to near-NVFP4 precision for legal work
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Lawyer’s eight-V100 AI server moves DeepSeek from 2-bit to near-NVFP4 precision
A lawyer in Columbia, South Carolina, upgraded his private AI server to improve precision and performance. Using eight Nvidia V100 GPUs, 1TB of RAM, and an RTX 3090, he moved 80% of his work from 2-bit to near-NVFP4 precision, claiming it matches the model’s official 4.25-bit weights. The change reduced crashes linked to a faulty PSU and improved fidelity metrics, though code output slowed by 3–30% and legal writing by 9–23%. Testing showed higher accuracy in next-token prediction and reduced KL divergence, with 95.1% matching Nvidia’s reference model. The system now handles two requests simultaneously, boosting total output to 159 tokens per second. RAM upgrades to 128GB modules resolved ECC errors, but GPU speeds remain capped. Plans include adding eight more V100s and a second server for parallel tasks. The lawyer, Nick Mermiges, founder of PLI Labs, aims to scale further while keeping data on-premises.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Tips to Dry Clothes Indoors Without Raising Energy Bills
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Drying clothes indoors? Stop condensation and musty smells without sending your energy bills soaring
Drying clothes indoors during cold months increases home humidity, causing condensation, mold, and musty odors. Chris Michael of Meaco offers solutions to dry laundry efficiently without raising energy bills. Tips include spinning laundry thoroughly in the washing machine, ventilating rooms with open windows, using airers instead of radiators, and arranging clothes to allow airflow. A dehumidifier can remove moisture without losing heat, with a Meaco Arete One 10L costing 24p per load compared to £1.01 for a tumble dryer. Annual savings of over £200 are possible with frequent use. Everyday actions like keeping saucepan lids on and opening windows during bathing also reduce indoor moisture. Proper drying methods prevent damp smells and preserve energy efficiency.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Researchers Link Chinese AI Models to Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Researchers allege DeepSeek, Kimi, and other Chinese AI models were trained using banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
Researchers from UnemploymentLabs claim Chinese AI models like DeepSeek V4, Kimi K3.1, MiniMax-M3, and Ling-3.1-Flash were trained using Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, despite U.S. export restrictions. Their analysis focused on weight initialization patterns during model training, comparing statistical distributions of random values generated by Blackwell chips with those of the models. By replicating the initialization process with identical hardware and software configurations, they found matches in shader module (SM) counts—148 for Blackwell B series—and thread counts of 2,048 per SM. Altering these parameters disrupted the correlation, confirming the models' use of Blackwell hardware. While the study does not prove illegal export violations, it highlights the chips' role in training these models. AMD cards were ruled out for DeepSeek V4 after analyzing weight value patterns, as they failed to replicate the same statistical distribution. The findings underscore the challenge of enforcing export controls on AI hardware, as companies may still access Blackwell chips through rentals or other means.
